Part two. WeWork. In August twenty nineteen, WeWork filed to go public, and for the first time, everyone could see the numbers. The year before, it had lost about one point nine billion dollars. The filing also showed something strange. Adam owned stakes in buildings that he leased back to WeWork. And a company he controlled had trademarked the word We, and WeWork paid it nearly six million dollars for it. He later gave that money back. Investors panicked. The forty-seven billion dollar valuation started to melt. Talk dropped to twenty billion, then even lower. In September, Adam stepped down as CEO, and the IPO was cancelled. SoftBank rescued the company, and Adam left with a package reported at over a billion dollars. Follow for part three.
